pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
plugin routing/redirection/removal/deprecation support for collections

* collection runtime metadata
* collection load hooks (currently used for metadata load and Ansible version checks)
* transparent recursive redirection of migrated plugins from core (or a collection) to a collection
* dynamically shimmed target-side redirection of migrated Python module_utils
* transparent import support for formerly core Python modules that have been moved to collections (eg 3rd party plugins that import from migrated module_utils)
* deprecation metadata and runtime warnings for collection plugins
* necessary support to kill task_executor prefix-based network action substitution
* rewritten collection Python loader for more standards-compliant behavior and better testability

TODO:
- [ ] Better warning/error handling (eg when a target collection is missing)
- [ ] Confirm usage of SpecifierSet for `requires_ansible`, decide vendor or dep on `packaging`
- [x] Decide if deprecation is date-based, version-based, or support either/both (final answer: both are supported, but future sanity will enforce one or the other, not both concurrently).
- [x] Increase test coverage
- [x] Fix broken Python 2.7 support
- [x] Fix bytes/text string handling throughout
- [x] Sanity cleanup
- [x] Fix broken integration/unit tests
- [x] Restructure/share core + collections metadata loading to minimize AnsibleCollectionLoader deps
- [x] Fix disabled ansible-doc "bad fragment" test in collections
- [x] Figure out how to implement pre-release support for SpecifierSet validation (eg, `requires_ansible: >= 2.10` doesn't include 2.10.0b1)
- [x] Bikeshed metadata naming
- [x] Bikeshed location of `requires_ansible` key
- [x] Issue deprecation warnings for migrated/redirected content
- [x] Collection loader: importing from module_utils/foo/__init__.py does not work #68872
- [x] Collection loader loads and executes module code, causing problems with old libraries in path #68701
- [x] Confirm this fixes https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/68223
- [ ] ~Powershell/CS module_utils shimming support~ (deferred)
- [ ] ~Solve warning spam (marshal from worker on existing queue)~ (deferred)

fixes #60424
fixes #68872

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
PluginLoader (et al)

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
This PR implements a new `meta/` directory for collections to contain various metadata about the collection. Currently a single file named `runtime.yml` will be read from this directory the first time the collection is referenced/loaded. A sample is located in the collections integration test, at `test/integration/targets/collections/collections_root_user/ansible_collections/testns/testcoll/meta/runtime.yml`.

The file may contain:

* a `requires_ansible` key, whose value is a PEP440 SpecifierSet that describes which versions of Ansible are supported by the collection (ala `setup.py` `python_requires` key, see https://packaging.pypa.io/en/latest/specifiers/) 
* a `plugin_routing` key, with child dictionaries keyed by plugin type (ie the subdir name under plugins), which contain child dictionaries of unqualified plugin names (since they're scoped to the the containing collection). A plugin name dictionary can specify:
  * `redirect: (target FQCN)` to redirect requests for that plugin to the named target plugin in this or another collection
  * `deprecation:` to issue a deprecation warning when a deprecated plugin is referenced (see collections test sample referenced above for usage)
  * `tombstone:` to cause a fatal error when a removed plugin is referenced (see collections test sample referenced above for usage)
* an `import_redirection:`  key to opt specific python module names into Python loader-level redirection (allowing the source name to be directly imported by code in the Ansible controller process, eg, external plugins)

A version of `runtime.yml` also exists under `lib/ansible/config/ansible_base_runtime.yml` that applies to the `ansible.builtin` synthetic collection, and should be used to record the locations of all plugins migrated out of Ansible. This metadata is consulted when referencing the `ansible.builtin` collection (eg unqualified usage of 2.9 core modules), and also as a "last resort" for any unqualified module usage before plugin resolution is failed- basically, this is the file that should keep everything working for <= 2.9 content running on >=2.10 when the migrated collections are present.

I vote strongly that it is in `galaxy.yml`... if not, then we will be introducing yet another metadata location that collection maintainers will have to add (probably in yet-another-subdirectory). For simpler collections, having to add a ton of extra files just for structure makes it not very fun.

Also, why not use the [same key that was used for roles](https://galaxy.ansible.com/docs/contributing/creating_role.html#role-metadata), `min_ansible_version` (that is, if it's defining a minimum, and not a range selection—it seems that would be the case according to the example like `>= 2.10`. However, if we are allowing more complex ranges (e.g. greater than 2.10 but less than 3.0) then that variable name would not be very accurate.

Would collection maintainers have to learn the syntax for defining [PEP440 SpecifierSet](https://packaging.pypa.io/en/latest/specifiers/)s? If so we should definitely document common uses, including:

  - greater than or equal to an Ansible version (matches `min_ansible_version` use from galaxy roles).
  - between Ansible version X.Y and A.B
  - exactly (and only) Ansible version X.Y
  - Ansible version 2.10 and later, up to 2.11 (similar to the second point I guess... but it looks like there's easier syntax for that versus 'up to arbitrary version'

issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
During some refactoring I tried to rename `plugins/module_utils/crypto.py` to `plugins/module_utils/crypto/__init__.py` in community.crypto, assuming that this does not change behavior for any module using this module_utils. Unfortunately, that does not work: while `from ansible_collections.community.crypto.plugins.module_utils import crypto as crypto_utils` works fine, `from ansible_collections.community.crypto.plugins.module_utils.crypto import CRYPTOGRAPHY_HAS_X25519` makes the task fail with:
```
fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! => {"msg": "Could not find imported module support code for openssl_privatekey.  Looked for either CRYPTOGRAPHY_HAS_ED448.py or crypto.py"}
```

As @abadger pointed out, there are explicit tests in ansible/ansible which test this for module_utils inside ansible/ansible itself:
* https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/test/integration/targets/module_utils/library/test.py#L60
* https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/test/integration/targets/module_utils/module_utils/spam6/ham/__init__.py

There seem to be no similar tests for collection module_utils, as these will apparently fail.

CC @mattclay @nitzmahone 

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
collection loader

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```paste below
devel
probably also 2.9
```

@felixfontein Non-empty `__init__.py` files are something we actually test for in the sanity tests because they're not supported. Including one in a collection results in an error:

```
ERROR: Found 1 empty-init issue(s) which need to be resolved:
ERROR: plugins/module_utils/crypto/__init__.py:0:0: empty __init__.py required
```

Ah, that's good to know! I never came that far since I didn't try running any tests except integration tests locally, and these already failed because of this.

I've now also found it in the docs: `Note that importing something from an ``__init__.py`` file requires using the file name:` (https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/docs/docsite/rst/dev_guide/developing_collections.rst). Sorry for missing that...

@mattclay i don't think we can do that.  Putting things in `__init__.py` files is a very central feature of python.  I've tried to keep things out of `__init__.py` in core because it prevents using namespace packages down the road, but it serves some very useful purposes, such as the backwards compatibility that felix was working on when he ran across this in the first place.

Since collections are even more outside of the ansible scope than what was in core, it policies won't apply there and people will want to do this even more.  So i think this needs to work for collections just as i supported it working in ansible/ansible when i wrote ansiballz
Nitzmahone also acknowledged this as a bug when i talked to him on Monday.  He had written an integration test for it but commented it out with a note to fix it later but forgot about it.

@abadger I didn't mean to suggest we shouldn't allow it. I only meant to point out that it's currently something that is reported as an error in the `empty-init` sanity test. Aside from that and the collection loader issue, there may be other areas that don't support it well, at least in tests.
